about: 78 hook structures for posts, emails and talks. Major Arcana are big-idea hooks. Cups are story and feeling. Wands are contrarian and bold. Swords are questions and challenges. Pentacles are numbers, proof and results.
example_founder: Every example is written as Wren, a fictional breathwork teacher who runs small retreats. Her numbers are invented to show the shape. Use your own true numbers.

positions.label: What they believe
positions.note: The belief your reader walks in with.

positions.label: What they'll do
positions.note: The move they make after reading.

cards.name: The First Day
cards.structure: Day one of {new thing}. I'm scared of {fear} and doing it anyway. Here's the first step: {step}.
cards.example: Day one of running retreats without a co-host. I'm scared of the empty room and doing it anyway. Here's the first step: I booked the house.
cards.when_to_pull: You're starting something and want people to watch it grow.

cards.name: The One Woman Show
cards.structure: Welcome to my one woman show, where I {role one}, {role two} and {role three} before {time}.
cards.example: Welcome to my one woman show, where I lead the breathwork, cook the lunch and answer the DMs before 10am.
cards.when_to_pull: You want them to see the real scale of what you hold, with a wink.

cards.name: The Receipt
cards.structure: Receipt for {result}: {item one}, {item two}, {item three}. Total: {the true cost}.
cards.example: Receipt for my first sold-out retreat: 40 voice notes, 3 rewrites of the sales page, 1 cry in the car. Total: 11 months of showing up.
cards.when_to_pull: You have a result and want to show what it really took.

cards.name: The Guest Check
cards.structure: If {your offer} were a dinner, here's the bill. Starter: {small win}. Main: {big shift}. Dessert: {the bonus nobody expects}.
cards.example: If my six-week breath course were a dinner, here's the bill. Starter: you sleep through the night. Main: you stop bracing in meetings. Dessert: your partner notices first.
cards.when_to_pull: You're explaining an offer and want it to taste delicious, not technical.

cards.name: Too Busy
cards.structure: Too busy {doing the thing you love} to {the thing everyone says you should do}.
cards.example: Too busy holding space for twelve women to post three times a day.
cards.when_to_pull: You want to name a boundary your audience secretly wants too.

cards.name: The Hotline
cards.structure: If you called my hotline at {late hour} about {problem}, here's what I'd tell you: {advice}.
cards.example: If you called my hotline at 2am about the retreat nobody has booked yet, here's what I'd tell you: it's a story problem, not a pricing problem.
cards.when_to_pull: Your audience has a late-night worry you can answer in one breath.

cards.name: The Front Page
cards.structure: Breaking news: {someone just like them} {did the surprising thing}. Here's how.
cards.example: Breaking news: a breathwork teacher with 900 followers filled her retreat in nine days. Here's how.
cards.when_to_pull: You have a win that deserves a headline. Keep it true.

cards.name: The Plot Twist
cards.structure: I thought {the problem} was {the wrong cause}. Then {the moment}. It was {the real cause} all along.
cards.example: I thought my empty classes were a marketing problem. Then a student said she never knew when they were on. It was my booking page all along.
cards.when_to_pull: You learned something the hard way and they still hold the old belief.

cards.name: The Permission Slip
cards.structure: This is your permission slip to {the thing they feel guilty wanting}. Signed, {who you are to them}.
cards.example: This is your permission slip to charge for the circle you've hosted for free for two years. Signed, someone who did it and kept every friend.
cards.when_to_pull: Your audience needs to hear yes before they can buy.

cards.name: The Quiet Room
cards.structure: Nobody talks about the quiet part of {experience}: {the honest moment}.
cards.example: Nobody talks about the quiet part of running retreats: the Monday after, when the house is empty and you wonder if it mattered.
cards.when_to_pull: You want depth over noise. Good for slower, softer weeks.

cards.name: The Full Circle
cards.structure: {Stretch of time} ago I was {old state}. Today I {new state}. What turned it: {turning point}.
cards.example: Three years ago I was teaching in a borrowed yoga room. Today I host in my own studio. What turned it: I stopped discounting.
cards.when_to_pull: An anniversary, a milestone, or a before and after.

cards.name: The Fine Print
cards.structure: The fine print on {popular advice}: it only works if {the hidden condition}.
cards.example: The fine print on 'just post every day': it only works if you have something to say every day.
cards.when_to_pull: Your niche keeps repeating advice that leaves out a condition.

cards.name: The Pause
cards.structure: Stop {what they're doing right now}. Before you {next action}, ask yourself {one question}.
cards.example: Stop scrolling retreat venues. Before you book a single villa, ask yourself who you want in the room.
cards.when_to_pull: Your audience is rushing and needs one beat of stillness.

cards.name: The Ending
cards.structure: I'm ending {thing you used to do}. Here's why, and here's what I'm doing instead: {new way}.
cards.example: I'm ending my free monthly circle. Here's why, and here's what I'm doing instead: a smaller paid circle where I can hear every woman.
cards.when_to_pull: You're closing a chapter, an offer or an old habit, in public.

cards.name: The Recipe
cards.structure: My recipe for {result}: {ingredient one}, {ingredient two}, a pinch of {ingredient three}. Leave out {the thing everyone adds}.
cards.example: My recipe for a calm launch week: one email a day, one live, a pinch of silence. Leave out the countdown timer.
cards.when_to_pull: You have a method you can share as steps.

cards.name: The Confession
cards.structure: Confession: I {thing they'd never guess}. And it's the reason {benefit to them}.
cards.example: Confession: I still get nervous before every session. And it's the reason I never rush a client.
cards.when_to_pull: You want closeness. Admit something human.

cards.name: The Collapse
cards.structure: {The thing} fell apart {when}. Here's what was left standing: {what held}.
cards.example: My retreat venue cancelled six weeks out. Here's what was left standing: every single booking, because the women came for me, not the pool.
cards.when_to_pull: Something broke and it taught you what only a break can teach.

cards.name: The North Star
cards.structure: Every decision in my business answers one question: {your guiding question}
cards.example: Every decision in my business answers one question: will this help a woman breathe easier in her own home?
cards.when_to_pull: You want to show your values without a lecture.

cards.name: The Night Shift
cards.structure: What I think about at {late hour} before {big moment}: {the thought}.
cards.example: What I think about at midnight before a retreat: did I pack enough tissues, and will they let themselves rest?
cards.when_to_pull: Late-night honesty. Lovely under a full moon.

cards.name: The Golden Hour
cards.structure: The best moment of {experience} isn't {the expected moment}. It's {one small true moment}.
cards.example: The best moment of a retreat isn't the closing ceremony. It's day two, when someone laughs for the first time.
cards.when_to_pull: Sell the feeling by pointing at one small, true moment.

cards.name: The Verdict
cards.structure: I've tried {option A} and {option B}. My verdict for {who}: {the choice}, because {reason}.
cards.example: I've tried in-person and online breath courses. My verdict for new mothers: online, because nobody should need a babysitter to breathe.
cards.when_to_pull: Your audience is stuck choosing. Make the call for them.

cards.name: The Whole World
cards.structure: Imagine {future moment}. You {dream outcome}. Here's the first thing that has to be true: {first step}.
cards.example: Imagine next spring. You're running your first retreat with a waitlist. Here's the first thing that has to be true: you tell people it exists this month.
cards.when_to_pull: You're inviting them into a bigger future. Strong at the open of a launch.

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.title: The First Feeling
cards.structure: The first time I felt {emotion} about {topic}, I was {where you were}.
cards.example: The first time I felt truly safe in my body, I was lying on a studio floor with my hand on my belly.
cards.when_to_pull: You want to open with a memory they can feel in their chest.

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.title: The Two of Us
cards.structure: {A client} and I both {shared experience}. Only one of us {the difference}. Now {what changed}.
cards.example: My student and I both grew up holding our breath at the dinner table. Only one of us had words for it. Now she does too.
cards.when_to_pull: You and your reader share a past. Name it.

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.title: The Circle
cards.structure: Three women walked into {place}. One {state}, one {state}, one {state}. Here's how they left.
cards.example: Three women walked into my circle on Sunday. One grieving, one burnt out, one just curious. Here's how they left.
cards.when_to_pull: You run something communal and want them to picture the room.

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.title: The Unopened Gift
cards.structure: You've had {resource} the whole time. You just haven't had {what was missing}.
cards.example: You've had a calm nervous system the whole time. You just haven't had ten quiet minutes to find it.
cards.when_to_pull: Your reader thinks she's missing something she already has.

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.title: The Spilled Cup
cards.structure: I lost {thing}. Here's what I didn't lose: {what remains}.
cards.example: I lost my biggest corporate client in June. Here's what I didn't lose: the morning practice that built the business in the first place.
cards.when_to_pull: A loss you can talk about with a steady voice.

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.title: The Childhood Memory
cards.structure: When I was {age}, {memory}. I didn't know it then, but it was {lesson for your work}.
cards.example: When I was seven, my grandmother taught me to count my breaths in thunderstorms. I didn't know it then, but it was my whole method.
cards.when_to_pull: You want to show where your work really started.

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.title: The Daydream
cards.structure: Close your eyes. It's {time} and {sensory detail}. That's what {offer} feels like.
cards.example: Close your eyes. It's 7am, the sea is loud and nobody needs anything from you. That's what my spring retreat feels like.
cards.when_to_pull: Selling an experience. Let the senses do the work.

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.title: The Walk Away
cards.structure: I walked away from {good thing} because {deeper reason}.
cards.example: I walked away from a full timetable at a big studio because I wanted to know every name in the room.
cards.when_to_pull: A choice that shows what you value more than money or status.

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.title: The Wish
cards.structure: If I could give every {audience} one thing, it would be {gift}. Here's how to give it to yourself: {how}.
cards.example: If I could give every new founder one thing, it would be a slow morning. Here's how to give it to yourself: move the first call to 10.
cards.when_to_pull: Generous, warm, useful. A gift post.

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.title: The Happy Ending
cards.structure: {A client} came to me {before}. Last week she sent me this: {her words}.
cards.example: A student came to me unable to sleep past 3am. Last week she sent me this: 'I woke up and it was light outside.'
cards.when_to_pull: You have a client's words and her permission to share them.

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.title: The Love Note
cards.structure: A love note to the woman who {situation}: {message}.
cards.example: A love note to the woman who booked the retreat and is now terrified to come: we saved you the window seat.
cards.when_to_pull: Someone in your audience is wobbling. Write to her directly.

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.title: The Grand Gesture
cards.structure: I {bold kind act} for {who}. Here's what happened next.
cards.example: I refunded a client who had finished the whole course because she lost her job. Here's what happened next.
cards.when_to_pull: A story where your values cost you something and paid you back.

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.title: The Hostess
cards.structure: If you came to {your space} tonight, here's how I'd welcome you: {ritual}.
cards.example: If you came to my studio tonight, here's how I'd welcome you: warm socks, ginger tea and no small talk for the first ten minutes.
cards.when_to_pull: You want them to feel held before they've booked.

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.title: The Steady Hand
cards.structure: When {a client} is {hard moment}, I always say: {the line}.
cards.example: When a student panics mid-session, I always say: 'You don't have to do anything right now. I've got the room.'
cards.when_to_pull: Show your calm under pressure in one sentence.

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.title: The Spark
cards.structure: Unpopular opinion: {belief that goes against your niche}.
cards.example: Unpopular opinion: you don't need a bigger audience to fill a retreat. You need twelve women who trust you.
cards.when_to_pull: You hold a view most of your niche would argue with.

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.title: The Fork
cards.structure: Everyone in {niche} is choosing between {A} and {B}. I chose neither. I chose {C}.
cards.example: Everyone in wellness is choosing between going viral and going quiet. I chose neither. I chose a weekly letter to 300 women.
cards.when_to_pull: You found a third way through a tired either-or.

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.title: The Horizon
cards.structure: In {timeframe}, {prediction about your niche}. Here's how to get ready now.
cards.example: In two years, nobody will book a retreat from a flyer. They'll book the woman they've watched for six months. Here's how to get ready now.
cards.when_to_pull: You can see where things are going. Say it first.

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.title: The Celebration
cards.structure: I'm celebrating {the thing most people would hide}.
cards.example: I'm celebrating my smallest launch ever. Six women, and every one of them finished.
cards.when_to_pull: Reframe a 'small' result as the win it is.

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.title: The Argument
cards.structure: {Common advice}? I disagree. Here's what I do instead: {your approach}.
cards.example: Post at peak times? I disagree. Here's what I do instead: I post when I have something true to say.
cards.when_to_pull: A rule your audience follows that you quietly break.

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.title: The Victory Lap
cards.structure: I {achieved result} without {the thing everyone thinks is required}.
cards.example: I sold out my autumn retreat without a single paid ad.
cards.when_to_pull: A true result that breaks a myth. Only if you can show it.

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.title: The Stand
cards.structure: I will never {thing others in your niche do}. Not even if {the temptation}.
cards.example: I will never run a fake countdown timer. Not even if it doubles the sales.
cards.when_to_pull: Draw your line in public. It attracts the right women.

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.title: The Fast Track
cards.structure: Stop {slow habit}. Do {faster move} today and you'll {result} by {when}.
cards.example: Stop redesigning your logo. Write the welcome email today and you'll have a waitlist by Friday.
cards.when_to_pull: Your reader is busy being busy. Hand her the shortcut.

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.title: The Last One Standing
cards.structure: Everyone told me to quit {thing}. I kept going because {reason}.
cards.example: Everyone told me to quit in-person workshops. I kept going because some things need a room.
cards.when_to_pull: Stubbornness that turned out to be wisdom.

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.title: The Heavy Load
cards.structure: You don't need more {thing}. You need less {other thing}.
cards.example: You don't need more content. You need less noise between you and the women who already love you.
cards.when_to_pull: Your audience is overloaded. Give her permission to drop something.

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.title: The Dare
cards.structure: I dare you to {small brave action} this week. Tell me what happens.
cards.example: I dare you to say your price out loud on a call this week, then stay quiet for five seconds. Tell me what happens.
cards.when_to_pull: You want replies. A dare gets them.

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.title: The Charge
cards.structure: If you've been {waiting situation}, stop waiting. Here's your next move: {move}.
cards.example: If you've been planning your retreat for a year, stop waiting. Here's your next move: put a deposit on the date.
cards.when_to_pull: Momentum post. Short, hot, one action.

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.title: The Hot Take
cards.structure: {Thing everyone admires} is overrated. {Underrated thing} is where the magic is.
cards.example: Big launch weeks are overrated. The quiet emails in between are where the magic is.
cards.when_to_pull: Flip what your niche celebrates.

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.title: The Rule Breaker
cards.structure: I broke the biggest rule in {niche}: {the rule}. Here's what happened.
cards.example: I broke the biggest rule in coaching: I published my prices. Here's what happened.
cards.when_to_pull: You did the forbidden thing and it worked.

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.title: The Sharp Question
cards.structure: What would {outcome} look like if {constraint} didn't exist?
cards.example: What would your business look like if you never had to post again?
cards.when_to_pull: Open a door in her head with one clean question.

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.title: The Crossroads
cards.structure: Which one are you right now: {state A} or {state B}?
cards.example: Which one are you right now: tired from too much work, or tired from the wrong work?
cards.when_to_pull: You want comments. Make them pick a side.

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.title: The Sore Spot
cards.structure: Does it still sting when {painful moment}? Read this.
cards.example: Does it still sting when a friend books someone else's retreat? Read this.
cards.when_to_pull: Name the private hurt, gently, then help.

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.title: The Rest Test
cards.structure: When did you last {restful act} without {guilt trigger}?
cards.example: When did you last take a full day off without checking your bookings?
cards.when_to_pull: Rest-themed weeks, the dark moon, integration.

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.title: The Cost
cards.structure: What is {habit} costing you? Count it: {what to measure}.
cards.example: What is saying yes to every discovery call costing you? Count it: hours this month, and how many became clients.
cards.when_to_pull: Make an invisible cost visible.

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.title: The Crossing
cards.structure: What would it take to move from {where she is} to {where she wants to be} in {time}?
cards.example: What would it take to move from one-to-one sessions to your first group in ninety days?
cards.when_to_pull: Lead into a plan, a course or a programme.

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.title: The Sneaky Habit
cards.structure: Are you {self-sabotaging behaviour} and calling it {nicer name}?
cards.example: Are you hiding from your launch and calling it 'refining the offer'?
cards.when_to_pull: Call out a pattern with love and a smile.

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.title: The Tight Spot
cards.structure: Stuck between {A} and {B}? There's a third door: {C}.
cards.example: Stuck between burning out and earning less? There's a third door: a smaller, higher-touch offer.
cards.when_to_pull: She feels trapped. Show the exit.

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.title: The 3am Question
cards.structure: What keeps you up at night about {topic}? Mine was {your worry}.
cards.example: What keeps you up at night about your business? Mine was 'what if nobody comes.'
cards.when_to_pull: Trade a fear for a fear. Builds trust fast.

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.title: The Last Time
cards.structure: If you {repeat the pattern} one more time, what will it cost you? Here's the way out: {way out}.
cards.example: If you push your retreat date back one more time, what will it cost you? Here's the way out: pick the date and sell into it.
cards.when_to_pull: She's looping. Lovingly break the loop.

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.title: The Quiz
cards.structure: Quick test: {question}. If you {answer}, {what that means}.
cards.example: Quick test: can you describe your offer in one sentence a stranger would understand? If you paused, that's your homework this week.
cards.when_to_pull: Playful diagnosis. Good for stories and polls.

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.title: The Challenge
cards.structure: {Number}-day challenge: {simple action} every day. Who's in?
cards.example: Five-day challenge: one minute of slow breathing before you open your inbox. Who's in?
cards.when_to_pull: Build a little community moment before an offer.

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.title: The Clear Eye
cards.structure: Would you {buy, book or trust} {your own offer} if a stranger described it the way you do?
cards.example: Would you book your own retreat if a stranger described it the way you do?
cards.when_to_pull: Founder-to-founder posts about sales pages and offers.

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.title: The Judge
cards.structure: Three questions to ask before you {big decision}: {question one}, {question two}, {question three}
cards.example: Three questions to ask before you hire a retreat venue: can I hear the sea, can I hear myself think, can I afford to lose the deposit?
cards.when_to_pull: Lend her your judgement for a big call.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.title: The First Coin
cards.structure: My first {sale, client or booking} came from {unexpected source}.
cards.example: My first retreat booking came from a voice note I sent to a woman I met at a market.
cards.when_to_pull: Show how small and human the beginning was.

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.title: The Juggle
cards.structure: {Number} {things} in {time}, while {constraint}. Here's the split: {breakdown}.
cards.example: Two retreats and one course in a year, while raising a toddler. Here's the split: retreats in spring and autumn, the course runs itself in winter.
cards.when_to_pull: Show the real calendar behind the result.

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.title: The Craft
cards.structure: It took me {number} {attempts} to get {thing} right. Here's version {number}.
cards.example: It took me nine drafts to get my welcome email right. Here's version nine.
cards.when_to_pull: Share the finished thing and honour the drafts.

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
cards.title: The Keeper
cards.structure: I kept {number} of my {number} {things} and let go of the rest. Here's what stayed: {what}.
cards.example: I kept three of my eleven offers and let go of the rest. Here's what stayed: the retreat, the course and the circle.
cards.when_to_pull: Simplifying. Show the cut and the keep.

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.title: The Lean Month
cards.structure: My hardest month made {amount}. Here's what I changed the month after: {change}.
cards.example: My hardest month made 900 dollars. Here's what I changed the month after: I asked past clients what they'd pay for.
cards.when_to_pull: A low point with a real fix. Only your true numbers.

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.title: The Fair Exchange
cards.structure: Here's exactly what {price} gets you: {item one}, {item two}, {item three}.
cards.example: Here's exactly what 1,400 dollars gets you: four nights, every meal, two breath sessions a day and a room of your own.
cards.when_to_pull: Doors are open. Make the price feel fair and clear.

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.title: The Long Game
cards.structure: {Number} {weeks or months} of {consistent action}. This is what it built: {result}.
cards.example: 52 Sunday letters in a row. This is what it built: a waitlist of 180 women.
cards.when_to_pull: Proof that steady beats loud.

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.title: The Practice
cards.structure: I've {done the thing} {number} times. Here are the {number} things I'd tell my first-time self.
cards.example: I've led 400 breath sessions. Here are the three things I'd tell my first-time self.
cards.when_to_pull: Authority without a brag. Mastery as a gift.

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.title: The Garden
cards.structure: From {small start} to {result} in {time}. No {shortcut}.
cards.example: From one Tuesday class to a full studio in two years. No ads, no investors.
cards.when_to_pull: A growth story with roots.

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.title: The Legacy
cards.structure: {Number} women have {result} with {method}. Here's what the ones who changed most had in common.
cards.example: Ninety women have finished my course. Here's what the ones who changed most had in common.
cards.when_to_pull: You have a body of work. Mine it for a pattern.

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.title: The Ledger
cards.structure: I tracked {metric} for {time}. Here's what the numbers said: {finding}.
cards.example: I tracked where every booking came from for a year. Here's what the numbers said: seven in ten came from email.
cards.when_to_pull: You kept score and found something surprising.

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.title: The Steady Climb
cards.structure: Month one: {number}. Month three: {number}. Month six: {number}. The only thing I changed: {change}.
cards.example: Month one: 4 students. Month three: 11. Month six: 26. The only thing I changed: I taught on the same day every week.
cards.when_to_pull: Show a trend line in plain words.

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.title: The Abundant Table
cards.structure: What {result} paid for: {meaningful thing one}, {meaningful thing two}, {meaningful thing three}.
cards.example: What my spring retreat paid for: my mother's flights, a new mat for every student and a full week off.
cards.when_to_pull: Money talk with warmth. Show what it makes possible.

cards.name: King of Pentacles
cards.title: The Bottom Line
cards.structure: The one number I watch every week: {metric}. Here's why it matters more than {vanity metric}.
cards.example: The one number I watch every week: replies to my letter. Here's why it matters more than followers.
cards.when_to_pull: Teach her what to measure.
